column1: # A possible implementation order for P/04: a plan, not a norm or a reduction of the lesson checklist. Read all norms and imported contracts in full.
# Single-chapter address 4 maps to acceptance/scenarios.tsv and acceptance/seams.tsv, not acceptance/4/.

# gate uses the P/01 grammar: seams:4:<cases|*>, accept:4:<cases|*>, vectors:<own package>, vectors:<owner>/<package> (a package of another owner with a consumers.tsv row whose consumer is 04-controller), code:*, build (the profile build); checks separated by ;.

# seams runs acceptance/seams.tsv through the seam adapter over the real implementation code. accept selects only acceptance/scenarios.tsv, which the judge runs on the process stand; never seams.tsv. All former gates keep holding.
# code:* — the rows of forms/code-rules.tsv whose stage is this stage or a stage of a smaller n hold, under the closed dictionary of the code
# checks Platform/common/acceptance/forms/code-rules.tsv; the generation cycle checks them, not the acceptance; * is
# the only argument; a row is a data error when neither its stage nor a stage of a larger n has code:* in its gate.
# weight relative 1–5; depends lists earlier n; when=true applies always.
# forms/slot-fate.tsv and forms/slot-release.tsv name the decisions. A selector alone does not prove the process.

# Common vectors remain assigned by common/vectors/consumers.tsv and their package README row/field selections; a vectors:<owner>/<package> gate runs all assigned tables of the package. Do not replace them with local tests.
# The accept scenarios start the resource (P/05) and most use the console doors (P/06): their gate stands at controller_stand, which waits for these lessons;
# an item stands at the stage of its subject, and its full-stand scenarios remain evidence in its text.
# norms — elements separated by «; »: the sections of the norms, the forms and the packages the stage builds on (read in full, above), and the items of the readiness
# checklist of spec/04-controller.norms.md (the lines - [ ] **P/04-MM**), written P/04-MM (a lesson without chapters); each item stands in the norms of exactly one stage,
# the stage at which every subject of the item exists; an item at no stage or at two stages is a data error. The items of the system
# checklist of spec/04-controller.norms.md stand at no stage: they need the OS, a host or several lessons.
# A checklist item is assigned where its behaviour is built; its process-stand evidence still runs at controller_stand.
# Admission builds move/sync and durable recovery; snapshots builds publication/counter effects; pass_report composes those steps.
